_meta.title: Prisoners who are foreign citizens, Europe
_meta.what_it_measures: How many people in prison are citizens of another country, and what share of all prisoners they are. value = foreign prisoners as % of all prisoners in the latest year available (computed here from the two published numbers).

fields.eurostat.<year>: foreign_number, national_number, total_number and the same per 100,000 inhabitants, as published
fields.raw_cells: cells as printed (NA = not available, NAP = not applicable, *** = see report)

notes: Keys are ISO3; the UK is published in three parts and is keyed GB-EAW (England and Wales), GB-SCT (Scotland), GB-NIR (Northern Ireland) - ISO 3166-2 style, not ISO3. Kosovo = XKX.

Spain and Bosnia and Herzegovina: SPACE I also gives separate prison administrations (Spain: State Administration, Catalonia; BiH: state level, Federation, Republika Srpska); kept under space_i_sub_administrations of ESP/BIH.

Eurostat and SPACE I count at different dates and with different national definitions; do not mix years from the two without care. Eurostat data in fact come from the same national prison administrations (UNODC/Eurostat questionnaire).
SPACE I reports before 2021 (2000-2020, PDFs on the same page) also have foreign-prisoner tables in other layouts; not parsed here.
SPACE I: "Data for which the data validation procedure could not be achieved is presented between square brackets." Such cells are listed in bracketed_codes (their numbers are kept).
SPACE I rows printed with no figures at all (e.g. Malta and the BiH administrations in 2021) are not in the PDF table as data and so are absent here.
Country names broken across lines in the PDFs were rejoined by table order (see FIX in the script).
